purpose: Resolve by measurement the contradiction between two committed records about the C/AES-NI toolchain, and replace the Coordinator's declared-unmeasured throughput sizing with a measured figure.

contradiction_resolved.record_a: ledger/questions/RQ-AES-001.yaml constraints: records gcc 13.3.0 with -maes as available
contradiction_resolved.record_b: ledger/goals/GOAL-AES-001.yaml next_action: records a GF(2^8) census leg blocked because 'neither numpy nor a small C program is installed'
contradiction_resolved.finding: Record A is correct about the C path. gcc 13.3.0 compiles and links AES-NI intrinsics (-maes -msse4.1) and the binary runs. Record B's parenthetical is wrong about the C program specifically; numpy is separately confirmed absent. NEITHER COMMITTED RECORD IS EDITED — this receipt is the correction of record.
contradiction_resolved.caveat: This measures the toolchain, not the census leg. Whether that leg is feasible also depends on its memory profile, which is not measured here.

method: 20000000 AES-128 block encryptions, full 10-round schedule via _mm_aesenc_si128/_mm_aesenclast_si128, sequential dependency chain (no pipelining across blocks), CLOCK_MONOTONIC, gcc -O3 -maes -msse4.1. Source committed alongside as throughput_bench.c.
consequence: Exhaustive or near-exhaustive search is not merely infeasible here; the entire campaign budget reaches 2^42.6 against 2^128, short by a factor of 2^85. Any full-round result obtainable under GOAL-AES-002 must therefore be STRUCTURAL — an argument validated at reduced scale and in analogues — not computational. This is now a measurement rather than the unmeasured sizing recorded in DEC-20260731-019 limitations.
not_established: Four-core scaling is assumed linear, not measured.
This says nothing about memory-bound workloads, which is where the MITM/biclique-style tables actually bind.
It says nothing about AES security and licenses no cryptanalytic claim.
